name: Islamic Studies
description: Encompasses the study of Muslim and Islamic artistic, cultural, historical, intellectual, linguistic, literary, philosophical, political, religious, sociological, and scientific presence and impact on human society over the past one and a half millennia.
notes: No more than two courses may represent the same area of study.
Each student must attend three lectures on topics relating to Islamic Studies and submit a brief 1–2 page write-up for each.
All courses must be taken for a letter grade with a grade of C or above.
No courses taken Credit/D/Fail may be applied toward the certificate.
Language courses and non-Yale courses may not count toward the certificate.
No more than two course credits may overlap with a major, simultaneous degree, or another certificate.
No course credit may be applied toward the requirements of more than two curricular programs.
Graduate and professional school courses may count toward the certificate.
Declare on Yale Hub by January 15 or September 15 of the final semester at the latest.
